advisories.title: The withdrawal is correct, but its justifying clause 'no value survives its own publication' is overbroad -- v1.9's own narration publishes surviving counter-examples
advisories.finding: v1.9 states the withdrawal is made 'because no value survives its own publication', and the operation value repeats 'it has no value that survives its own publication, let alone the next edit'. The first clause is false as an absolute: values scoped to a frozen byte state survive publication indefinitely, and v1.9's own defect narration publishes two of them ('resolved v1.7 holds 8, resolved v1.8 holds 11') -- both of which I verified and both of which will still be true in a century. The freeze text I measured (7.2.2.1(a), at e1cdb71d...) likewise names surviving forms: 'true with itself included -- or scoped explicitly to a state that excludes it ("as of the predecessor", "excluding this block")'. A fixed point also exists mechanically: the sentence contributes a constant number of occurrences whatever digits it states, so a stable in-document count is computable at emit. The TRUE and load-bearing half of v1.9's argument is the second clause -- any such figure breaks on the next edit touching the token -- and that fragility argument alone justifies withdrawal.
advisories.why: Freeze 7.2.2.1's vacuous-caveat discipline: recompute limitations and justifications, not just claims. This one is a justification that overclaims impossibility where the honest claim is fragility.
advisories.notABlockerBecause: No false measurement is published; the act the clause justifies is valid on the surviving (fragility) ground, which v1.9 also states; and the withdrawn statement's replacement makes no claim about v1.9's own bytes at all.
advisories.environmentCaveat: I resolved 7.2.2.1(a) at MY measured freeze digest. The freeze moved repeatedly on 2026-08-12 and v1.9 pins no freeze digest, so I cannot know whether the scoped-form wording predates v1.9's authoring; the counter-examples inside v1.9's own bytes are therefore the load-bearing evidence, and they alone carry the finding (per 7.8.1).

advisories.title: Stage 3's alternation says 'bytes' and the corpus writes 'Byte': same-kind byte-length figures inside the excluded prefixes are asymmetrically excluded
advisories.finding: The 31 add-backs are recordBytes (19), digestBytesHex (7) and droppedCount (5). Inside the same excluded prefixes sit canonicalJsonByteLength (7), preimageByteLength (7), startByte (2) and endByte (2) -- quantitative, hard-comparable figures of the same kind as recordBytes -- which the /bytes/ alternation does not match because their keys carry 'Byte' singular. If recordBytes belongs in the class (v1.8 listed two recordBytes rows among its verified-unaffected members, so the corpus treats it as class-relevant), its 18 siblings-in-kind belong too.
advisories.notABlockerBecause: These are figures about the measured DATA, not self-measurements of the artifact -- outside what the class exists to derive, and outside every completeness claim v1.9 makes. The asymmetry costs coherence, not coverage of the mandated block.
advisories.repair: Extend the alternation with |byte (or enumerate byteLength|startByte|endByte), or publish the class extension and let the member list be the definition.

advisories.title: Qualitative self-measurements are structurally outside the quantitative class -- named here so they are not rediscovered as if concealed
advisories.finding: The counting rule is quantitative by construction, so self-measurements that state no figure are not members: findingIdentity.workedVectors.pairAssertions[0..3].measured (four measured equality assertions; the key is literally 'measured' but key name only operates inside the excluded prefixes, and these are outside them); preservationOfV15.rule ('NOTHING was forced. The claim is MEASURED here, not asserted: each carried key is serialised with sorted keys from both documents and compared.'); placeholderCensusMeasuredHere.measuredBy; and shasumCrossCheck.mismatchExamples = [], an empty array asserting zero examples in the exact block the v1.8 review's A-R18-01 flagged as carrying the real assurance weight. All are recomputable claims a future auditor should reach, and none is reachable through this class.
advisories.notABlockerBecause: v1.9's completeness claim is explicitly and honestly scoped: 'Coverage of the QUANTITATIVE leaves in that block is complete' -- measured TRUE. It nowhere claims the class reaches qualitative self-measurements. The dispatch's attack was for a self-measurement the basis 'still misses' against what it claims to catch; these sit outside what it claims.
advisories.repair: A successor could add a second, enumerated register of qualitative self-claims (the four blocks above), or extend stage 3 to operate outside the excluded prefixes too, where it would add pairAssertions.measured and measuredBy at zero cost to the published counts' recomputability -- at the price of re-deriving them.

advisories.title: Three residual definition gaps, none of which defeated reproduction, all of which the published extension would close at once
advisories.finding: (1) 'Added back' is not pinned to a pool: read as restoring rule-qualifying excluded leaves it reproduces 31/898 exactly; read as promoting ANY excluded-prefix leaf by key it gives 48/915. The natural reading wins the hard comparison, but v1.8's 59 fell to exactly this kind of freedom. (2) The exclusion taxonomy is not exhaustive: adversarialControls and staticClosureFixtures are measured-object blocks left inside stage 1, so CLASS = 898 over-includes data leaves -- the safe direction, and consistent with 'it is still only an instrument', but '898' should not be read as a census of self-measurements. (3) measuredSelfReportLeavesTotal = 41 holds under the corpus scalar-leaf convention (the v1.8 review counted the same 41); an instrument counting empty containers finds 42, the extra leaf being mismatchExamples = []. My class-figure reproduction is invariant to this choice; the coverage TOTAL is not.
advisories.repair: Publish the extension -- the 898 member paths -- as the v1.8 review already recommended. A published member list makes all three residuals unarguable simultaneously and converts every future recount into a set diff.
